 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajeev Ranjan Prasad
 Oral Order
3 06-06-2024

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the informant and learned APP for the State.
2.

The petitioner has filed the second anticipatory bail application in connection with Mahila P.S.
Case No. 32 of 2021 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that earlier the petitioner had filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 52105 of 2021 but when the said application was taken up for consideration,
on a wrong instruction, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner informed the Court that the petitioner is on Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.32789 of 2024(3) dt.06-06-2024 police bail.

In view of the said submission, this Court directed the learned court below to consider the prayer for bail of the petitioner in the light of the judgment of this Hon'ble Court in Mahendra Prasad Singh Vs. State of Bihar reported in 2004 (3) PLJR 491.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that it is well settled that the litigant should not suffer for the fault on the part of the lawyer, therefore, if this application is not entertained and heard, the petitioner would suffer irreparable loss and injury.

5. Mr. Siya Ram Sahi, learned counsel for the petitioner agrees at the Bar that when the anticipatory bail application of the petitioner was heard on 06.04.2023 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.
52105 of 2021, the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner had informed the Court that the petitioner was on police bail which was not a correct fact.

6. In the aforesaid background, this Court directs to call for a legible carbon/photostat copy of the case diary and the injury report of the informant in connection with Mahila P.S. Case No. 32 of 2021 from the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Patna Sadar, Patna.
